s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and pain over the clavicular area with a tender mass and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: 6-month history of swelling and moderate pain over the left clavicular area
Tender 2 × 3 cm swelling over the left clavicle with erythema
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h
Midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture
key_facts: 9-year-old boy
6-month history of swelling and pain
No fever, weight loss, or trauma
Received unspecified oral medications for one month
Normal vital signs
Tender swelling over the left clavicle
Small clean overlying wound and erythema
Preserved shoulder range of motion
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Normal complete blood count, renal and liver function tests
Unremarkable abdominal ultrasound
Midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Tender swelling over the left clavicle, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and presence of a small clean overlying wound and erythema

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic swelling and pain over the clavicular area with a tender mass and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring nature of osteomyelitis and presence of a tender swelling over the left clavicle

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture and presence of a tender swelling over the left clavicle

raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, along with the absence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which can present with bone lesions and localized symptoms.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more aggressive symptoms and systemic signs such as fever and weight loss

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Usually associated with signs of infection such as fever, discharge, and elevated white blood cell count, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Typically involves multiple sites of infection and often has a more prolonged and complex course

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Usually presents as a painless, expansile bone lesion without the inflammatory signs seen in this patient
